blocks.text: An anomalous goods and services broker primarily based in London, England, with satellite offices in Hong Kong and New York. Catering to the super-rich, with extensive political and financial ties worldwide (particularly within sub-Veil communities), this group has caused extensive problems for the Foundation. Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. is known for collecting rare and obscure items, along with providing its clients the most exclusive, expensive, and rare experiences available, no matter the cost to human life.

These activities have resulted in conflict with the Foundation on numerous occasions. The group is not known for the use of force; they prefer to apply extreme financial and political pressure to achieve their goals. When forced to use more direct means, Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. employs outside agents, often nameless contractors embedded within hundreds of layers of shell companies. This makes it difficult to understand the true of their activities in the mundane and paranormal worlds, particularly where their executives are involved.

Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. has caused several SCP containment breaches, primarily through the use of money or social pressure. Many reports, records, and even anomalies have been leaked by Foundation personnel, influenced by the promise of large amounts of money or the threat of blackmail.

Information pertaining to Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd., such as the name of the director or even a list of members, has proven very difficult to acquire. Agents encountering members of this group are advised to maintain a cover story and not reveal, for any reason, their Foundation ties or any SCP information. Double-agents are advised not to get comfortable with the life Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. affords those affiliated with them, as these privileges can and will be taken away if they are discovered.

blocks.text: The Global Occult Coalition (GOC) was founded after the conclusion of the Seventh Occult War , a covert conflict taking place during World War II. The victorious Allied Occult Initiative recruited defectors from the defeated Axis powers to establish a new organisation, tasked with protecting humanity and concealing the existence of the anomalous. The GOC regard themselves as the police of the paranormal world, responsible for the elimination of any "parathreat" they identify.

Although the GOC is a political force affiliated with the United Nations, they are lead by the Council of 108, consisting of the most influential organizations in the paranormal community. This diverse group of occultists, psychics, priests and scientists includes the Bavarian Illuminati, the Knights Templar, the Servants of the Silicon Nornir, the International Center for the Study of Unified Thaumatology (ICSUT), the World Parahealth Organization, and Goldbaker-Reinz Ltd. These groups supply the GOC with advanced experimental technology , as well as expertise in Applied Thaumatology , which are both utilized by the GOC's PHYSICS Division to detect and destroy anomalies.

The GOC and the Foundation share many of the same goals and adversaries, which has enabled the coordination of joint operations in the past. However, while the GOC has enough respect for the might of the Foundation to avoid open conflict, they object to the Foundation's practice of containing SCP objects, and GOC operatives in the field will strive to neutralize anomalies before the Foundation can recover them. Although overt confrontation of this group must be avoided, GOC agents are to be treated with suspicion at all times.

blocks.text: Sarkicism is a religious/philosophical system that encompasses a variety of traditions, beliefs, and spiritual practices largely based on teachings attributed to “Grand Karcist Ion”, its deified founder. Adherents practice ritual cannibalism, human sacrifice, corporeal augmentation, thaumaturgy, and dimensional manipulation. Highly secretive, the general public appears to have no direct knowledge of their existence; the one exception being the CotBG, who views them in apocalyptic terms. Organic manipulation has allowed certain Sarkicites to achieve anomalous states of being, transcending the physical limitations of baseline humans. Disease is viewed with reverence and Sarkic shrines have been discovered with offerings of swollen lymph nodes and tumorous growths. Sarkic cults treat contagions as consecration, a means to "cull the weak" and purify the masses, and thus actively seek to ensure their spread.

The Foundation divides known Sarkic cults into two distinct strands: Proto-Sarkic and Neo-Sarkic. Proto-Sarkic cults can be found in insular communities throughout Eurasia's most isolated regions, its followers generally poor (if self-reliant) and hostile towards outsiders. Such groups eschew modernity, display acute technophobia, and are bound by superstition and taboo. In contrast, Neo-Sarkic cults are cosmopolitan, publicly embracing modernity and showing no apparent qualms with technology; their public lives differing little from others of their culture and social status. Adherents are primarily affluent families, rich in history and scandal.

Ultimately, it is believed that the Foundation only knows a fraction of what Sarkicism is and what its followers intend. Based on the available information, the speculated goals of Sarkic cults represent an SK-class dominance shift, including the possibility of an XK-class end-of-the-world scenario.

profileContent.title: The Church of the Broken God

blocks.text: The Church of the Broken God is a dualistic religion that worships mechanization, regarding "flesh" as fundamentally flawed. They believe that their god has been shattered and requires reassembly, and that each of them will undergo their own apotheosis after this divine reconstruction. The church has access to multiple technological anomalies, and members of the group are frequently anomalously augmented by mechanical prosthetics, so their attempts to spread their faith more widely present an ongoing threat to Normalcy.

While similar beliefs were present in the ancient Chinese Xia Dynasty , the origins of the group are generally traced back to the founding of the Mekhanite Empire in Mycenaean Greece. Conflict with contemporaneous states , including the Daevite and Sarkic Empires, resulted in its destruction during the Bronze Age Collapse. Survivors founded the City-State of Amoni, which lasted until the 1st Century BCE. The theology of these states outlasted their demise, influencing and being influenced by Christian Gnosticism, and eventually making a resurgence during the Industrial Revolution.

The church in its modern form is divided on the question of how the reconstruction of their god is to be achieved. The largest extant denomination, the Broken Church, pursues the physical reassembly of Mekhane by bringing together anomalous artifacts, and have identified multiple SCP objects as pieces of their deity. Their leader, Robert Bumaro , has demanded that the Foundation hand over these objects to his church, and has lead multiple attempts to recover them by force. The Cogwork Orthodoxy separated from the Broken Church during the 19th Century, under the influence of wealthy industrialists, to pursue individual mechanical augmentation through a process known as "Standardization" , notably rejecting any incorporation of modern electronics. A more recent breakaway movement was founded by a woman known as "Saint Hedwig", with her Church of Maxwellism focusing on augmentation through digital technology . Maxwellists believe that by connecting together all members of the church, the collective will of humanity can "recompile" the Broken God, which they refer to as WAN. Due to their presence online and connections to Silicon Valley, Maxwellism is the most rapidly growing faction of the Church of the Broken God, despite ongoing efforts by the Foundation to limit their reach.

blocks.text: During the 20th century, a number of high-value assets and personnel split off from the SCP Foundation, calling themselves the " Chaos Insurgency ." To this day, they remain one of the Foundation's most notorious enemies — with the overarching goal of razing the organization to the ground, and the Veil of Normalcy with it.

In pursuit of the destruction of the normalcy doctrine, no price is too great for the Insurgency. The Insurgency frequently resorts to acts of extreme violence or outright terrorism to further their goals. The organization is known for an ethos of " starting enough fires to exhaust the fire brigade ," relentlessly sabotaging the Foundation to expose vulnerabilities. While most members of the Insurgency are ordinary individuals, the organization frequently makes use of anomalous items to their own benefit, especially those stolen from the Foundation .

The Insurgency overall functions as a decentralized network under which numerous cells of revolutionaries , freedom fighters, research institutes, and intelligence centers fight against the Foundation. However, at its center is the secretive "Delta Command," led by an anonymous individual known as "The Engineer." Their base of operations remains unknown.

The Insurgency's ideology is unclear, thanks in no small part to their own disinformation. Internal propaganda describes the organization as freedom fighters, uplifting the common people against the oppression of the Foundation. The Insurgency at its core seems to champion anarchist, anti-state, and radical left-wing politics, though they will frequently make use of cells from all political backgrounds.

Personnel are remain cautious of possible raids, terrorist action, and spies from the Insurgency, and are to notify their superiors about any activities from fellow personnel fitting the Insurgency behavioral profile.

blocks.text: The Unusual Incidents Unit was formed after the onset of the Cold War, when many aspects of the American Government were focused on utilizing the anomalous and preventing the communists from doing the same. This led to the creation of a special FBI division devoted to rapid response to paranormal events and crimes. Director J. Edgar Hoover was personally involved with their creation.

Although initially given significant funding and resources by the American Government, following the end of the Cold War and the dissolution of enemy organizations such as the GRU-P, the UIU had been in a state of decline for many years.

Disparagingly referred to as "X-Files" and " UIUseless " by the larger anomalous community, the agency is generally well meaning, but due to a lack of financial resources, little manpower, and bureaucratic obstruction by the US Government, it is often perceived as ineffective. The influence of the Foundation and Global Occult Coalition in the United States Government has stopped the UIU and other USGOV entities dealing with anomalous activity, such as US Air Force's 616th Squadron ("Roswell's Revengers") and US Navy SEAL Team Bravo Papa Romeo Delta, from being dissolved entirely.

FBI Agents and Special Agents who join the Unusual Incidents Unit often have backgrounds in psychology, STEM fields, and art studies. As part of the PATRIOT act, agents of the unit are required to be administered Personalized Memetic Silencing Agents (PMSA, colloquially referred to as 'gag orders' by agents of the UIU) to avoid leaks.

The Unusual Incidents Unit has been known to engage in combat alongside and against various anomalous organizations in the past, including participating in several combat operations under Foundation supervision in the 1950s and 1960s, and the "Black Mamba" incident in Afghanistan in 1976, an infamous skirmish between UIU agents and members of GRU-P.

Currently, a division of the Unusual Incidents Unit oversees the autonomous anomalous state of Three Portlands . An example of underfunding and understaffing in the Unusual Incidents Unit can be seen in its sole remaining division in the Midwestern United States .

blocks.text: The Serpent's Hand is a small but formidable organization responsible for several security breaches. At least three different individuals have been encountered, all of whom used possible or confirmed anomalous items for infiltration purposes (including SCP-268 , which was stolen from the Foundation, who had in turn recovered it during a raid of a Chaos Insurgency facility ). The total number of members belonging to this organization is unknown, as is their level of technology, number of possible SCPs held, or total level of threat. However, it is clear they are highly coordinated and possibly dangerous. One of their leaders is thought to be a figure known as "L.S.", who is considered to be personally responsible for two security breaches in Foundation sites.

The Foundation currently has very little information about the Serpent's Hand, and almost all known information about the Serpent's Hand has been leaked from the GOC intelligence. The group seems to embrace the use and existence of paranormal items, and in particular seems to embrace humanoid and sentient SCPs. The Serpent's Hand has been highly vocal in criticizing the containment and destruction of these SCPs, especially those which are fully human and are not particularly destructive.

The group seems to have unfriendly relations with the Chaos Insurgency and the ORIA , and an extremely hostile relationship with the GOC. The only recorded cases of unprovoked violence by Serpent's Hand members have been against GOC agents.

The Serpent's Hand seems primarily based in an anomalous location called the Wanderers' Library, a building accessed through portals found in many different parts of the world. Direct assaults on the Library have so far proven unfeasible, even when entrance could be found. However, initial intelligence seems to suggest the Hand has little understanding or control over the place.
Attempts to infiltrate the Wanderers' Library are ongoing.

Links to the Factory have been speculated but are unconfirmed.

blocks.text: "This church is to other churches what clowns are to people. There are some superficial similarities, but all the wrong things are being emphasized and exaggerated so you can't quite put your finger on what is wrong... Sure, it isn't out to get you, but what does it mean? Why is it there? What happens if it calls to you?" —Dr. █████

The Fifth Church, also known as the Church of Fifthism or the Fifthist Fellowship, is a highly secretive religious organization which possesses ties throughout the entertainment industry. Despite repeated investigations, culminating in the 2007 nationwide sting known as "Operation Stargazer", no further details regarding its doctrines, its practices, its number of members, or its goals have been confirmed, although a watchlist is maintained of 100 confirmed and suspected Fifthist celebrities and other prominent personalities. Its origins have been placed in varying points in the mid-20th Century and various locations in North America and Asia, but some sources have dated it to centuries earlier.
The Fifth Church has never communicated directly with the SCP Foundation, but is to be considered a hostile force.

However, it is not known if this is the work of a single person or multiple agents of a single, unknown agency. blocks.text: Very little conclusive information has been recovered about the person of interest called the Black Queen. She claims the given name " Alison Chao ", the name of the daughter of researcher Dr. ██████ Gears and ██████ ███ Chao before Gears' recruitment by the Foundation.

The Black Queen possesses unusual knowledge of Foundation structure and activities, and contained anomalies. The reason for this unusual knowledge has yet to be conclusively identified, but it appears to be gained partially through anomalous means (including the possibility of extra-universal information sources). She has repeatedly been able to breach Foundation security utilizing this information, in addition to classified anomalous means.

Conflicting reports exist of the Black Queen's activities and motivations (likely due to multiple individuals or deliberate counter-intelligence). Initial reports characterize her as malevolent, murderous, and destructive. Other reports characterize her as neutral or benevolent. All intelligence indicates her hostility towards the Foundation.

There are reports of the Black Queen's involvement with most major Groups of Interest known to the Foundation, along with several world governments. Unverified sources claim that she is the same individual as L.S. of the Serpent's Hand, and that L.S. stands for "Little Sister". The reason for this unusual close connection is possibly due to the Black Queen's use of the Wanderers' Library .
Intelligence indicates the presence of multiple other individuals also calling themselves "the Black Queen". The nature and origin of these individuals is inconclusive.

blocks.text: Based out of the Three Portlands location of interest, Anderson Robotics first came to the Foundation’s attention in 2007 with the capture of SCP-1360 . Specializing in the sale of anomalous androids, robots, artificial intelligences, and cybernetics, the organization is led by a Three Portlands native and skilled thaumaturge named Vincent Anderson . Following its absorption of multiple assets from the now defunct Prometheus Labs, and its popularity within the Maxwellist Church, Anderson Robotics quickly gained a fair amount of traction in the realm of paratechnology within the 2000s and 2010s. Anderson currently uses Three Portlands as a shield, in addition to the group's remarkable espionage capabilities and overall popularity within the free port, to escape direct confrontation with the Foundation . The organization has increasingly come under scrutiny by the UIU for its various attempts to influence the United States Government, with Vincent Anderson himself a particular person of interest to their Three Portlands Field Office .

blocks.text: During the early 20th century, the Chicago Spirit was the largest anomalous criminal organization in the Western hemisphere. Based in Chicago, Illinois, the group's influence extended to most major cities in the United States, particularly New York, Boston, New Orleans, and the extradimensional city-state of Three Portlands . The Spirit was known for recruiting individuals with anomalous capabilities, as well as creating and exploiting anomalous artifacts for use in its criminal activities.

The Spirit was founded in 1895 by Chicago resident and bar owner Richard D. Chappell, who was himself an anomalous individual. Despite years of efforts, the Foundation remained largely unsuccessful in its attempts to suppress Chappell's rise to power, due in part to its limited resources at the time as a result of an ongoing internal crisis . In January of 1919, the Foundation officially suspended all opposition against the Chicago Spirit to ensure their cooperation in preventing the spread of SCP-2680 . Once allowed to operate unimpeded, the Spirit flourished into a nationwide syndicate and eventually became a driving force in the illegal distribution of alcohol during the Prohibition Era.

Thanks to the success of its bootlegging businesses, the Chicago Spirit continued to amass power over North American markets and politics throughout the 1920s, and the Foundation was eventually forced to terminate its truce with the group in order to prevent the complete dissolution of scientific normalcy. On July 11th 1933, Richard Chappell was finally apprehended by Foundation operatives following a raid on the Spirit's base of operations. In the absence of its leader, the group gradually destabilized, and most of its members and assets were acquired by other organizations . As of 1938, the Foundation officially considers the Chicago Spirit to be defunct.

However, rumors of the Spirit's continued survival have persisted in subsequent decades. Various artifacts have been discovered which imply the group's involvement, though a conclusive link has yet to be proven. Furthermore, recent evidence has revealed the emergence of a new syndicate calling itself "The Chicago Spectre", which seems to operate primarily in anomalous underground communities. Investigation into this group and its connections to the original Spirit (if any) are ongoing.

blocks.text: The Parawatch Wiki is an online web forum of conspiracy theorists, paranormal enthusiasts, and amateur writers, operating with the intent of investigating and exposing anomalous phenomena. The group primarily compiles short stories on their forum, detailing encounters with paranormal phenomena, historical cases, and any unusual events users have experienced. Further operation and any potential impact on normalcy is hindered by the geographic spread of the userbase and the lack of central coordination.

Despite investment in the paranormal, Parawatch has no knowledge on the nature of anomalous phenomena, the Veil, and the Foundation's existence. This in tandem with public obscurity has prevented them from potentially endangering the Veil. The group is currently being left active as a means of misinforming and misleading other investigations into the anomalous.

blocks.text: Wilson's Wildlife Solutions is a paranormal publicly funded wildlife service based in Clackamas County, Oregon, specifically in the town of Boring. Although the Foundation has known of Wilson's Wildlife Solutions' existence and anomalous affiliations since 1999, it took nine years until the Ursus Maritimus Incident in 2008, for their existence to be officially recognized and a relationship established between the two groups. Currently the Boring Agreement outlines that Wilson's Wildlife Solutions should be supervised by MTF Beta-4 ("Castaways"), local to Site-64, and that they may handle containment of Safe or Euclid fauna based anomalies with varying degrees of Foundation intervention (on a case to case basis). Amendments to the Boring Agreement can be, and have been, made to account for grey areas or new policies as necessary.

blocks.text: Founded in 1892, Prometheus Labs was dedicated to researching anomalous objects for use in developing new technologies. Over the years, Prometheus Labs developed into a multinational conglomerate selling advanced and anomalous technologies to governments, militaries, and Groups of Interest. Throughout its history, Prometheus Labs displayed a nominal amount of cooperation with Foundation efforts to protect normalcy, and at times even collaborated with the Foundation, but refused to cease its study of anomalies and resisted Foundation oversight.

In 1998, following a long period of financial decline, the Prometheus Labs conglomerate was dissolved, resulting in the creation of numerous successor companies formed from its subsidiaries. The breakup of the conglomerate was fraught with technical and administrative difficulties, resulting in the loss of many products and the layoffs of numerous personnel. Most of the former projects of Prometheus Labs now in containment were recovered during this time, and many of its former employees were hired by the Foundation.

blocks.text: "Gamers Against Weed" is a loosely-organized confederation of anomalous individuals, as well as associates thereof, that produce or procure anomalies for satirical purposes and/or for their own amusement. More recently, however, they have also been implicated in supplying anomalies to left-wing political organizations. While Gamers Against Weed organizes its activities primarily over internet channels, several real-world locations associated with the group have been identified and raided. Current intelligence suggests that Gamers Against Weed is in the process of creating and distributing a set of anomalous humanoids to parody Dr. Wondertainment's "Little Misters" series, and that it is aware of the Foundation's operations, if not its exact nature.

Detainment of Gamers Against Weed's members has proven more difficult than anticipated. Some of the group's organizers are believed to possess reality-altering capabilities, either in their own right or through access to outside resources. Current operations are focused on the containment of related anomalies and the identification and analysis of Gamers Against Weed's most dangerous members.

blocks.text: Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting is purported to be a circus of anomalous origin and purpose. Currently, there is no evidence that this group exists beyond the allegations of various sapient SCPs and a handful of damaged non-anomalous artifacts. Most related objects typified by humanoid status utilize anomalous deformities for the sake of performance in some way, such as SCP-1884 and SCP-2902 . Others appear to be typical fairground objets d'art , such as SCP-1921 , or take the form of 'attractions' for the show, such as SCP-3717 or SCP-1695 . Typically, objects related to Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting are found at fairgrounds where the show is said to have 'performed.'

A number of prominent figures in the anomalous world are Deer alumni, including Vincent Anderson, the CEO of Anderson Robotics, and Esther "lesbian_gengar" Kogan, one of the co-founders of Gamers Against Weed.

As the Foundation's operations in Three Portlands are heavily restricted by a number of agreements with the FBI's Unusual Incidents Unit, Deer College itself is relatively free of Foundation intervention; however, all Deer alumni are automatically marked as persons of interest, and may be subject to increased Foundation scrutiny.

blocks.text: The Shark Punching Center (also known as the Selachian Punching Center, The Shark Punching Centre, Selachiosk Pungix Combin , among others) is an organization located in one or more parallel universes, apparently acting as an alternate-universe counterpart to the Foundation. While the Foundation has known of the Center for several decades, the structure, documentation, and general tone taken by the Shark Punching Center varies wildly, suggesting one or more universes are in a state of flux.

Documents pertaining to the Shark Punching Center have been recovered, and indicate a much more militaristic and unstable tone than a Foundation document. As the name would suggest, the SPC is mostly focused on furthering hand-to-hand combat as a means to neutralize selachian entities, though some documentation fails to differentiate between "selachian" and "aquatic" .
It is unclear if the Shark Punching Center has any knowledge or concern of or with Foundation activities.

blocks.text: The Horizon Initiative is an organization created in the late 1960s by various influential sects in the main three Abrahamic religions as a response to the growing number of anomalous activities and groups which they perceived as threats. Though the full extent of their goals is uncertain, the Horizon Initiative is known to target SCP objects, either with the intention of retrieving or destroying them, depending on each item's perceived place in their dogma.

The Initiative is led by a tribunal composed of leaders from the three largest sects involved in its creation, though a large amount of internal strife often leaves the official leadership in less than full control of the organization. The HI's main combat force, Project Malleus, is generally deployed in anti-cult operations and in SCP retrieval operations.

The Initiative's relations with most other Groups of Interest and the Foundation seems to be in a state of constant flux; while all parts of the HI perceive the Church of the Broken God and Fifth Church with a great degree of hostility (and at times engaging them in armed conflict), sentiments toward the Foundation and the GOC vary greatly, from open hostility to a limited willingness to cooperate, depending on the internal affiliation of individual members.

blocks.text: Originally known as the ЧД АКН ("ChD AKN", or Fourth Department Abnormal Occurrences Commission), it was established in early 1935 by direct decree of J. V. Stalin, its first task being the investigation of the murder of S. M. Kirov.

During WWII, the Commission expanded into the newly reorganized GRU as Division "P" - Psychotronics, working to counteract anomalous threats from the SS, Ahnenerbe, and the Vatican, and to capture and study anomalous artifacts both at home and abroad for the benefit of the Soviet government. Division "P" has carried on with this role throughout the Cold War, making Foundation operations in the countries of the Comintern difficult.

After 1991, rapid restructuring, coupled with budget cuts and the decommissioning or sale of significant assets, resulted in numerous defections of their personnel (A significant proportion of both Chaos Insurgency and MC&D operatives in Eastern Europe originated from GRU Division "P" ranks) and the flooding of the European black market with anomalous items formerly in their possession. Currently, this Group of Interest poses little direct threat to the Foundation.

blocks.text: Established in 1971 as an interfaith humanitarian relief agency, recovered documents describe the Manna Charitable Foundation's mission as "sharing all of God's miracles with the least of His children". Funded indirectly through associations with various charitable groups and religious organizations, and on occasion publicly endorsed by wealthy philanthropists or academic institutions, the MCF's primary agenda since its founding has been the free distribution of anomalous objects, or their by-products, to civilians living in poverty-stricken regions in the Third World or in areas afflicted by warfare, famine, or natural disaster.

The MCF is currently recognized as a non-governmental organization by the United Nations, and is known to operate legally and illegally in several hostile or isolated regions outside the Foundation's sphere of influence. While no SCP objects known to have been distributed by the MCF to date have caused intentional harm to human beings or communities (and detained MCF operatives tend to demonstrate strong pacifist beliefs), containment breaches associated with the group have often resulted in human casualties or severe threats to the global status quo due to unforeseen consequences of the object's release from containment, and/or a zeal to distribute potentially "helpful" objects immediately without rigorous scientific study of their long-term behavior.

These restaurants specialize in anomalous food and culinary practices , and vary widely in variation and style. Despite the scale of the Ambrose Restaurants chain, they are generally non-hostile and will instead flee from threats directed towards them.

Ambrose Restaurants is currently believed to be jointly owned by persons of interest "Chaz Ambrose" and "Marius", but due to lack of public appearances this is unconfirmed. Notably, several groups of interest have engaged in relations with Ambrose Restaurants, including Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd. and Herman Fuller's Circus of the Disquieting , though the extent with which they collaborate is unknown. blocks.text: The Church of the Second Hytoth is an occult organization of human and alien entities that adhere to the extraterrestrial Ortothan religion, aiming to aid a universal guardian deity ("Rakmou-leusan") in combat against extrauniversal threats (known as "Voruteut"). The central beliefs of the religion are that the current universe, the "Second Hytoth," was preceded by a different universe, which used to exist until it was consumed by an extrauniversal entity. A group of survivors fled to the newly created Second Hytoth, our reality, with seven of them choosing to ascend to godhood to ensure the universe's safety. Six of these gods died over time, leaving Rakmou-leusan as the last survivor.

Operations taken by the Church are performed underneath the veil, likely to avoid heavy scrutiny from normalcy organizations. The main language of the group is the Ortothan Extraterrestrial Language (OEL), which has been anomalously kept unchanged despite the distances between Ortothan sects — group members attribute this to acts of divine intervention. Human Ortothan belief systems are known to have existed by ~11000 BCE, corresponding to the formation of the ancient Ortothan Kingdom civilization, though modern branches have only been developed in the past century. Ortothan groups separate from the Church exist, all being significantly smaller in comparison and tending to have differing moral beliefs.

Beyond the Church, the Ortothan religion has an interstellar and intergalactic presence, having initially emerged among extraterrestrial civilizations. Numerous such Ortothan civilizations are known to exist, with their full extent not yet ascertained. Among the largest of these is the Terzan 2 Ortothan Coalition, a collection of Ortothan entities residing in Globular Cluster Terzan 2 at war with the hostile "Twelve Stars" civilization. The only Ortothan civilization known to have entered the solar system is Species of Interest-002; it is presumed extinct.

blocks.text: The Office For The Reclamation of Islamic Artifacts (ORIA) is a paramilitary force, answerable only to the Supreme Leader of Iran, dedicated to the collection and utilization of anomalous artifacts throughout the Middle East and Central Asia. Following the 1979 overthrow of the Imperial Iranian government by revolutionary forces, and subsequent creation of the Islamic Republic of Iran, all Foundation personnel were expelled from Iran as "agents of colonialism." Attempts at maintaining a clandestine presence in the country met with failure, with the majority of Foundation personnel either captured or killed and Sites ██, ███, and ███ being captured by Iranian forces. To prevent Iran from being left behind in the field of extranormal research, the ORIA was created by a secret decree of Supreme Leader Khomeini in 1981. Despite its name, the group has not limited itself to the pursuit of anomalous objects of Islamic origin.

Although the ORIA has access to considerable resources, its effectiveness is hobbled by infighting among numerous factions within the organization. Some of these disputes center around philosophical differences, such as the weaponization of anomalous objects, while others appear to be personal in nature. The proliferation of factions appears to have been intentional, as the organization of the ORIA often leaves multiple commanders with overlapping areas of responsibility. It is theorized that the reasoning behind this arrangement was to prevent any one individual from accumulating enough power to pose a challenge to the Supreme Leader.

With the spread of Iranian hegemony throughout the Middle East and Western Asia, the ORIA has expanded its reach across the region, becoming the foremost paranormal organization in the Middle East. The ORIA is to be considered a hostile force, and Foundation personnel are advised to use extreme caution when engaging.

blocks.text: The Imperial Japanese Anomalous Matters Examination Agency or IJAMEA (not to be confused with the Foundation precursor IGAMEA, the Imperial German Anomalous Matters Examination Agency), was Japan's official and primary anomaly agency in the period from the Meiji Restoration in 1868 until the end of World War II in 1945. IJAMEA was founded with the purpose to bring Japan up to speed with Western esoterics research, acting as a modern counterpart to pre-existing so-called "primitive" groups. In this capacity, the IJAMEA catalogued hundreds of different anomalies spread throughout Japan and her colonies, conducted extensive research on these, and undertook numerous projects aiming to utilize the anomalous for the greater good of the fledgling Empire.

IJAMEA saw its most significant role during WWII, when it attempted to weaponize several anomalies to assist military forces in the war against the Allies. Rushed planning and insufficient funds, however, resulted in few of these programmes bearing fruit. The IJAMEA was formally disbanded with the Treaty of San Francisco in 1951, and most of its assets were either transferred to GOC control or covertly acquired by the Foundation.

However, imperial loyalists and Japanese nationalists within it kept IJAMEA alive in the post-War years, this time as a clandestine organization, during which its main focus was checking the spread of communist influence in Japan and East Asia. Today, it primarily serves to care for the well-being of Japan's diverse but faltering anomalous ecology, and supports various nationalist agendas with its ties to prominent politicians, businesspeople and cultural personalities throughout Japan. It seeks to return some political power to the Imperial family and return Japan to great power status, and actively seeks to exploit the various anomalies in its possession for this purpose. The Foundation is seen as a foreign rival at best, and agents are to exercise due caution when interacting with IJAMEA personnel.

The origins of the Valravn Corporation can be traced back to the fall of the legendary mercenary Jomsviking order and it is believed to have existed throughout history in various iterations. Valravn professes a syncretic belief in pagan Norse determinism combined with hyper-capitalism worship, which it uses to ideologically justify its mercenary business.

blocks.text: Very little is known about Alexylva University or its motives. Evidence appears to suggest that the organization exists in some sort of alternate universe in which Latin and Greek cultures maintain dominance at least over the Western Hemisphere; nothing to date is known about any other part of this world. All University-related objects have been found in the Mid-Southern United States, and more specifically in Tennessee , leading Foundation researchers to believe the University itself is located in that geographical area.

Many objects associated with the University (which is not believed to have built the objects) are recovered during postal transit via an agency known as "Phitransimun Combine" and accompanied by relevant paperwork, which has helped shed light on the objects and the place from which they came. To date, all that is known about the methods that transfer the objects is that the technology uses principles similar to that of the Einstein-Rosen Bridge, a concept considered purely theoretical by contemporary science. A particular section of the University known as the Department of Natural Philosophy is considered responsible for the transferences, possibly without the knowledge or consent of the rest of the organization.

blocks.text: Prior to the Convention on Preternatural Phenomena , several prenormalcy agencies oversaw the study and/or the containment of the anomalous. One such organisation was His/Her Majesty's Foundation for the Secure Containment of the Paranormal, also known as His/Her Majesty's Foundation for the Study of Curiosities and Phantasmagoria. One of the oldest paranatural organisations in history, His/Her Majesty's Foundation oversaw all paranatural phenomenon and threats across the British Isles and beyond, paving the way for many methodologies in anomalous research and containment.

In operation since the fifth century C.E., the group have been a secret pillar in British history, overseeing its several invasions, blossoming trade routes, industrial revolutions and its eventual height as the British Empire. However, following the Sixth Occult War, the group officially dissolved and joined with 12 other organisations to form the current Foundation. Though now seen as a relic of the past, their prior works have continued to be both hindrance and help to the modern Foundation. Even today, many of the anomalous objects and entities contained in the UK were inherited from this group.

blocks.text: The Wandsmen are a group of extradimensional journalists and archivists. They seek to explore the multiverse and uncover its mysteries, while spreading and preserving knowledge.

All members of this group undergo a transformation that gives them avian features and anomalous abilities. They also utilize a group of anomalous artifacts known as " Maps of the Multiverse " to travel through dimensions to study their locales and inhabitants.

In contrast to many groups of interest, the Wandsmen have attempted to work with the Foundation multiple times. One of their goals is the preservation of existence so they can study it, so they see the Foundation as an ally against the multiverse's destruction.

However, they have a variety of extremely dangerous members, have produced multiple anomalous items, and strongly object philosophically to the Foundation's desire to preserve normalcy and conceal knowledge of the anomalous.

blocks.text: Goldbaker-Reinz Ltd. is one of the foremost insurance providers for the anomalous world. It provides insurance to both individuals and institutions, as well as reinsurance, data vending, risk analysis, and forensic & enforcement services. It is known throughout the anomalous world for always honoring the letter of its contracts in good faith. It holds a seat on the Global Occult Coalition's Council of 108 due to the trust its predecessors gained from substantial recovery services provided in the wake of the Seventh Occult War, and it continues to provide services to the GOC, the Foundation, and many more.

The modern incarnation of Goldbaker-Reinz merged from Goldbaker Ltd., led by the enigmatic Goldbaker, and the Reinz Group led by Werner Reinz in 1981 after other founding members of the Reinz Group vanished in mysterious circumstances. The origin and full history of Goldbaker are lost to time, though individuals with similar titles or names have been providing similar services stretching back to the dawn of human civilization — and possibly beyond.

The Foundation has a number of outstanding contracts with Goldbaker-Reinz . Policies range from the mundane, such as standard personnel insurance health and life insurance, to the largely financial, such as providing beryllium bronze and other materials at fixed prices in the event of containment failure, to the rare and exotic, such as procurement of oxygenating algae in the event of a GH-Class Dead Greenhouse scenario. A number of these policies are redundant with the Foundation's own contingencies, but for two such risk averse groups such redundancy proves reassuring.

These contracts were entered into in good faith, but the Foundation also views them as a means of maintaining an accurate and up-to-date understanding of the inner workings of Goldbaker-Reinz. The Foundation is cognizant of Goldbaker-Reinz's position of power within the anomalous world, so the goal of contract negotiations is to minimize the money and information given while maximizing the coverage and information received. Despite this perennial game of cat-and-mouse, the Foundation and Goldbaker-Reinz still consider each other trustworthy — at least enough to conduct business.

blocks.text: One of a number of precursors to the Foundation as it exists today, the Commission on Unusual Cargo was established by the East India Company in 1623, for the purpose of containing and protecting its more peculiar cargo. It existed in this form until 1649, the year in which the group disappeared along with all of its assets, in response to a demand from the East India Company that they utilise the Unusual Cargo they had stockpiled to gain a military advantage against several large bands of privateers.

Subsequently operating in secret, the Commission continued to collect objects and entities until its merger with the Foundation in 1917. A number of these anomalous items were transferred into the Foundation's possession, along with Cargo Manifests describing the properties of and procedures for the safe storage of this cargo. This vast record of anomalous history is still being reviewed and digitised by Foundation archivists.

For as long as it was active, the Commission was headed by a merchant officer, the Right Honourable Othaniel Trower. It is unclear if this was a single, anomalously long-lived individual, or a series of multiple people using the same name. As the Commissioner of the organisation, he was overseen and advised by an eight member Board of Regents, and commanded a large staff of Wardens, Curators, and other operatives.

blocks.text: One of the most ancient and renowned academic institutions in the anomalous world, the Medician Academy of Occult Art (in Italian: Medicea Accademia dell’Arte Occulta) is a GoI based in Florence, Italy. Founded in the late 15th century by Lorenzo de’ Medici, lord of Florence and patron of arts; during the Renaissance, the Academy was able to spread its influence across most nations of Europe and the courts of the Old Continent. The activities promoted by the Academy included teaching art techniques and the recollection of old anomalous artifacts from ancient cultures.

From the mid 18th century, after going through a brief period of decadence, the Academy was able to recover and create new branches in new countries across new continents. The institution oriented its activity towards the recovery and restoration of artistical items, developing a peculiar taste for the arts. This led to hostile relations with the AWCY? movement, which is considered the main rival of the Academy.

- Anomalous News Publisher and business trust from a parallel universe. - Produces anomalies using information technology, which most of the time do not affect the physical bodies of those exposed to them. - Creates anomalous items with the appearance of normal information carriers (paper, disks, etc.). - Products are often dangerous, because the human capabilities required for using them are either overestimated or misjudged. - Structure, leaders and details of the world ECO Press is located in are unknown, although the history of both universes seems mostly the same. - Exists in a dystopian world where the ECO Press has taken over all the governments. - ECO Press has only a limited ability to view our universe. - Fluent in Chinese, but some members also know English. - Amicable towards the Foundation, since they only want to explore our universe. - Does not actively try to harm people.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown Asia Notexam Houses

- Organization wishing to reform human society using anomalous means, focusing on freedom of opinion, confidentiality of personal information, environmental protection and deindustrialization. - Founded during the First Industrial Revolution in Great Britain to fight the increasing mechanization, previously known as the Flower Art Committee. - Usually employs plant-based anomalies with memetic and cognitohazardous effects, distributed in random cities with a greeting card. - Complex organizational structure, secrecy on par with that of the Foundation. - Members mostly have anomalous abilities and are divided into the ranks of Guards, Fixers and Florists, the latter of which are the leaders. - Divided in two fractions, the Gardeners, who try to change society instantly through sacrifice and the Planters, who take a more subtle approach with satire and memes. - Fractions are not hostile towards each other and even work together on occasion. - Hostile towards the Foundation because of its means of acquiring information. - Tries not to harm people.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown The entire world Tnsbilws

- Organization specialized on anomalous logistics and transport of anomalies - Full name is GpExpress Logistics Ltd. - Formerly the logistics department of Marshall, Carter and Dark Ltd. but started operating independently in 2014. - The headquarters is in Portland, Oregon, but they operate worldwide. - Hires and collects anomalies to aid in transport of goods and people, can use containment procedures on par with those of the Foundation. - Security personnel protect the cargo with their lives, often occupying hostile forces long enough to bring it to safety. - Successfully defends themselves against all attempted interceptions by the Foundation, but makes no effort to prevent tracking. - GpExpress only cares about delivering its cargo intact, and doesn’t pay much attention to obstacles it has to remove to fulfil its deliveries.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: China China Areyoucrazytom

- Small organization well versed in the field of the anomalous. - Display complex understanding of Chinese Fengshui Geomancy and Alchemy, ancient Chinese culture and ceremonial tea, despite appearing as Taoists. - Anomalous objects of the Sect are usually anomalous areas, buildings/structures, literature and tools pertaining to Chinese alchemy. - Members are skilled at escaping, messages left behind by them are often written in lyrical form and require a lot of interpretation. - Tries to evade the Foundation. - Not above causing casualties.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: China China breaddddd

- Producer of video games for all platforms imaginable. - Normally products don’t have side effects, but their unique idea of game production leads to problems then and when. - The Foundation considers buying products for different uses, be it recreation or training. - LETTERS Entertainment has many different game developers, resulting in many different games, but they all influence reality in some way. - Some game developers seem to strive for being better than others. - Tries to evade the Foundation. - Takes the health of its customers into account.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown China Airalin_Knowledge

- Organization dealing with anomalous advertisements for anomalous products and their delivery. - Produces anomalous advertisements, but has no anomalous items themselves. - Products are often dangerous, because the human capabilities for using them are either overestimated or misjudged. - The Foundation is confronted with multiple versions of the same group, originating from different universes, as indicated by distinct differences between the versions as, for example, a different name. - Known to the Foundation by multiple names due to its multiversal nature, such as OB Media, Observe Media, Ooooo Bright! Media and others. - Leaders originate from different universes and are anomalous. - Advertisements tend to be intended for entertainment, and contain a certain amount of sarcasm. - Its advertisements can be harmful, but it is unknown if this is intended.
Schistosoma Protection Institute (SPI)
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Yunnan, China Mostly in China Archibald1

- Organization of eco-terrorists with the goal to be ignored and to protect rare animals. - Claims that anomalous organisms are part of the ecosystem, just like non-anomalous animals. - Amalgamation of several different organizations, of which RICPI is the most active, though there is a viewpoint suggesting that they are actually different departments of the same organization. - The constituent organizations are: RICPI (Rare Ignore Creature Protect Institute), Rick P. Breeding Research Base, Sacred Bloodstone Garden, SPI and Tan-Lu University. - Members' corpses are hosts to a variety of rare parasites, some known, some unknown to the Foundation. - Unknown organizational structure or leaders to the Foundation, due to RICPI's strong information control and misleading ability. - Infiltrated the Foundation, but will work with it on occasion to fight common threats. - Seems to put the well-being of its subjects above human life, but draws the line at a certain threshold.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: China China CatThorns

- Organization that cracks down on illegal and criminal acts using anomalous means in an extreme or even cruel way. - Disguised as a loose group of commonwealth organizations or criminal tool providers. - Hostile towards criminal actions. - Usually provides crime-related anomalies with hazardous effects on their users, distributed through trading. - Has deliberate behaviors to mislead how other GoI view them - Has two kinds of rumor about them: (1) SRUC regard themselves as a private club and their actions of violence recreational activities; (2) SRUC is an alternative commonwealth group composed of teenagers from anomalous communities.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Kowloon Walled City, Hong Kong, China China MScarlet

- Secondary school that possesses many anomalous objects, founded in 1952. - The campus was never located by the Foundation. - Aims to cultivate the most outstanding students through the application of anomalies. - Also teaches its students how to create anomalies. - Lead by an individual named "The Principal", adored by staff and students alike. - A lot of students later join anomalous organizations, the Foundation included. - Doesn't care about the Foundation. - Tries to keep its students and personnel from harm.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown China Fenrir Flamel

- Organization dealing in anomalous medicine. - Produces anomalous advertisements, but no anomalous items themselves. - Follows a creed that demands complete devotion from doctors towards their jobs. - Develops medicines and medical appliances using advanced technology. - Members support each other in their research. - Annoyed by medical research not up to their standards, and tries to rectify these inferior works. - Research is never published, but The Doctor provides its services to those interested in them. - Hostile towards the Foundation, trades them anomalous products in order to destroy it. - Tries to preserve human life.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown The entire world Areyoucrazytom

- Organization that combines characteristics of both religion and science fiction. - Has its own website (www.████████████.███). - Cult-like reputation. - Members of the Federation can link together through a form of hive-mind technology. - Creates deceptive memetic objects. - Unable to use their anomalous abilities effectively, failures tend to happen and cause damage. - Defenseless against the actions of the Foundation (or the local government). - Philosophy is a forced mixture of Buddhism and Space-Age Science Fiction, through which they try to prevent harm to others.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Guangzhou Guangdong China China Tnsbilws

- A forum to discuss illegal street racing, Operated by the TING team from Guangzhou and managed by the Maskman team and the FIREHIT team - There are illegal sales in the forum, and members from other organizations sell illegal vehicles and vehicle parts in the forum. - Forum members are highly mobile, and it is very difficult to track members of these organizations. - The TING team is good at collecting intelligence, the Maskman team is good at making unusual items, and the FIRHEIT team is extremely vulnerable to abnormalities. - The date of the forum's founding is unknown, but unreliable information indicates that the TING team itself has existed for more than three years. - Most of the SCPs are related to the "track" set by the forum, the "vehicle" for buying and selling, and the "driver" who has registered for the forum. - Cooperate with the SCP Foundation, but steal some information about the Foundation from time to time.

- Kingdom in parallel reality SCP-333-FR-PRIME, which is made of emptiness with a large floating island called the "The Kingdom". - Founded around 1820 but got cut off from the baseline universe by settlers returning to Earth until portal technologies were developed in the 20th century. - Denizens view themselves as superhuman and wish to claim the Earth because of their supposed moral superiority. - Technology of the Kingdom relies on anomalous phenomena and is superior to Earth’s technology. - Didn’t overrun the baseline universe because of internal problems. - Hostile towards the Foundation. - View casualties as necessary sacrifice, except for a persecuted group wishing to join with Earth's population in a peaceful manner.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: France France DrTesla and DrGemini

- Paranormal equivalent of the Gendarmerie, founded by Napoleon in 1804 to counter an alien invasion. - Struggles a lot today due to resources and budgetary cuts, can't go on strike because they don't officially exist. - Mostly concentrates on paracriminality, folklore and social issues at local scales. - Had a golden age in the 1900s and a dark age of collaboration under Vichy France. - Collaborates with the Foundation and with the official paranormal agencies of other states.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: France the entire world DrJohannes , Dr Grym , Mafiew

- Organization of unknown nature. Apparently formed by an ex-member of the Foundation in the early 2000's, themed around the work "20,000 Leagues Under the Sea". - Completely hostile towards the Foundation: the main goal of the organization is to wipe out the Foundation completely, for reasons still unclear to this day. - The organization acts through different means that make it hard to define clearly, such as memetic anomalies. - Create and use info-hazardous anomalies to specifically target Foundation personnel, and other entities collaborating with the Foundation. These anomalies seem to be designed to never hurt any non-Foundation related person.

blocks.text: Dinodon's Hand, a.k.a. Korean Serpent's Hand
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Korea (Joseon Dynasty) Korean peninsula Salamander724

- Korean branch of Serpent's Hand - Originally the "Underground Taoists" that deserted from the Joseon Dynasty's secret governmental agency in 1701. - First contact with Serpent's Hand (or the predecessor of the Serpent's Hand) was made in the USA in the 1910s, via Industrial Workers of the World. - Founded as the "Dinodon's Society" in 1919. - Fought against Imperial Japanese paranormal agencies by assisting the anarchic Korean resistance in the 1920s-30s. - Collapsed during the Korean War (1945-1953) and reorganised as "Dinodon's Hand" in the 1970s. - A woman named Hoya became its current leader in 2011. She is the daughter of SCP-953 . - Hostile to GOC, but tries to avoid the Foundation. - Politically anarcho-syndicalist. They distrust "para-capitalists" such as Marshall, Carter & Dark or Dr. Wondertainment. - Tries to avoid harming civilians, but can be ruthless towards operatives of the paranormal world if necessary.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Korea (Silla Dynasty), 841 Multiple worlds Salamander724

- Chŏnghæjin is a group of undersea drifters led by PoI "Jang Bo-go" , riding on "Makara", a semi-organic, semi-inorganic submarine “Makara”, which is also a giant humpback whale. - They attack colossal marine entities, called “Sea Deities”. This is because they believe that they can meet Pangloss who they call “Homa” again when they defeat all the sea deities, not sure why. - Their narrative essence is an eternal adventurer who marvels at things and people of the new worlds. “The struggle against the sea deities” is a MacGuffin to justify their eternal adventure voyage. You don't have to care about it actually. - They can go anywhere in the ocean. They can even go to the otherworlds via the underwater portals, which they call “Miryŏ”. They went to an otherworld in 1860, and returned to our Earth in 2021, after visiting various otherworlds. - The crews are undead who get life from the fire of Pangloss in place of the heart of Makara. When they go too far from Makara, they turn to dust and die. - The crew's ethnic makeup is very diverse and cosmopolitan, including parahumans from the otherworlds. Because they have recruited many shipwrecked people during their voyage for a long time. - Their stances on strangers are basically reciprocal. They engage in friendly trade with friendly strangers and ruthlessly retaliate against hostile ones. - The diacritics can be omitted as “Chonghaejin”.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Korea, early 1970s Mostly Korea POI_Damgi

- A group of incorporeal entities and ectomorphs. - Smaller precursors of the club merged together in the early 1970s. - Treats ghosts as human, and is against physicism and ectomorphic paranormal technologies such as SCP-2716 - Comprised of three branches: Human Resources, Management, External Affairs, each with its respective supervisors. - Members have various ages, backgrounds and causes of death. - Does not actively harm civilians, unless members are threatened first.
National Paranormal Emergency Service
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Korea, 2017 Korean Peninsular thd-glasses

- The presidential anti-anomaly organization of the Republic of Korea. - Established in December 2017, after the Joint Statement of December 5th . - Pursuit paranormal cases and illegal GoI in the Korean territory. - Does not have any abnormal assets, per the Joint Statement. Every anomaly they secured is given to the Foundation. - Despite all these restrictions, it has a capable intelligence network around the country and professional special forces which can handle risky cases related to anomalies.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: France, 1997 the entire world thd-glasses

- Environmentalists that wish to overcome the Second Law of Thermodynamics. - Emerged from the "Environmental Shelter Community" (ESC). - Stole information regarding ectoentropic objects from the Foundation, and created some themselves. - Views anomalies as a natural thing that people should accept. Oppose the destruction and the imprisonment of harmless anomalous objects. - Works divided into cells, each with their own task and goal. - Also try to aid people suffering from the anomalous, sabotage industry and conduct eco-activity through the use of anomalous objects. - Hostile towards the Foundation. - Tries to keep casualties as low as possible
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Korea, 2010s South Korea HS KHADYG , quilt , et al.

- Celeste is an enterprise that provides information, anomalous goods and services to private tutoring or other private institutes or develops educational businesses using them. - Celeste originated from the late 2000s when educational companies such as private institutes and publishers, which secured irregular means of business, formed a cartel. -The anomalous techniques involved are not believed to be very dangerous. - Mainly active in education complexes in Seoul. - Has numerous front companies and affiliate businesses.
The 10th Bureau, Korean Central Intelligence Agency (KCIA 10th Bu.)
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Korea, 1973 Korean Peninsular (No longer Active) thd-glasses

- Paranormal response agency under the KCIA of the 4th Korean Republic. - An attempt to directly control South Korean paranormal security, which until then had been handled by the Foundation. - Rather than research, the 10th Bu. focuses more on collecting instantly utilisable paranormal technology to keep the Foundation in check. - The 10th Bu. became a major competitor of the Foundation Korea Regional Command, hindering the Foundation's actions in South Korea. - Disbanded after the 5th Republic signed the Pearson Memorandum with the Foundation, handing over paranormal issues to the Foundation. - Most of its assets were absorbed by the Foundation, but some were scattered to other GoIs in Korea.
Noonday Oak Troupe (NOTE)
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Taiwan East Asia Z-cian

- Founded in 191█ by street performers - In the past, the Troupe held concerts to encourage people and to help the lower classes. - Today, NOTE creates anomalous music instruments that may or may not function properly. - Performs with its own creations, or donates them to the public. - Some performers seem to be anomalous beings. - Amicable towards the Foundation. - Wishes no harm, often asks the Foundation for damage control.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown East Asia, but sells worldwide lanlanmag

- Producer of anomalous video games. - Firstly detected by the Foundation in 20██. - Sell their products in the online game mall "██" which can't be accessed by the Foundation. - Little is known about PlugSoft, but it occasionally sends personnel to Foundation sites for "bug fixes". Apprehended individuals vanish after a while. - Apparently, there are many customers of PlugSoft, but the Foundation never located a player of its games. - Neutral towards the Foundation, although respectful. - Not completely immoral, but prioritise making money over other concerns.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: South Korea, 1970 East Asia Physique

- An anomalous large-scale company based in South Korea that pursues physical enhancement and prolonged lifespan. Currently active in East Asia. - Divided into three subsidiaries: Samdaecheon Fitness, which provides anomalous fitness equipment and personal training; Samdaechon Health care, which hunts spiritual animals and tests, sells anomalous drugs; and Samdaecheon Sports, which holds illegal fight clubs or partakes in escort services. - Originally was a group of trainers and biologists with anomalous technology, but the current CEO, Im Hanyeong, either killed or submitted them to change the group to be the corporation Samdaecheon today. - Remained the biggest criminal gang in Korea for a long time and is responsible for destroying the anomalous ecosystem of the Korean peninsula by indiscreet hunting. - The Foundation and the NPES' constant suppression attempts and the old age of the CEO made Samdaechon smaller, currently resembling a company more than a gang.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: South Korea. Around 1990-2000. World Wide Web romrom

- An online community of individuals related to anomalies. - The exact date of establishment is unknown. Rumours suggest it developed from a small chat room created between 1990 and 2000. - Accessible through an anomalous program called the "Horsehair Worm Program." - Divided into two separate communities called "Front Alley" and "Back Alley." - "Front Alley" is where individuals openly discuss their affiliated organisations. However, due to the low reliability of the verification method, it's uncertain if they are genuinely part of those organisations. - "Back Alley" allows activities under anonymity or fixed nicknames, resulting in more users than "Front Alley." - As is typical of online communities, anomalous objects are used/created for various purposes but are usually made to cater to user's interests and entertainment.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Large extradimensional cluster All dimensions with crustaceans, nematodes, or annelids and almost all dimensions around it SHARK_BYTES

- Consists of several thousand extradimensional fragments. - Invades other dimensions for survival. - Preexisting contact with the baseline universe, but discovered in 2020. - The Violet warps surrounding dimensions, making it easier to form interdimensional pathways. - All of the Violet creatures either are or resemble crustaceans, nematodes, or annelids. - Used to be active throughout the entire baseline, but currently mostly limited to Korea and its vicinity. - No permanent bases. If a location is depleted of resources, they move on to another one.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Parallel Universe No. 47 China Sigtina

- Association of a homo sapiens species called the Xingren, working towards gaining human rights and living space for their species, as their own world is dying. - Multifaceted organization, of which the R&D department is the most capable. - Proficient in crafting biotechnological anomalies. - Conflict may result in an SK Class Dominance Shift. - Are allowed to only trade with the Foundation. - Peaceful unless provoked.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Macau The entire World Nihilmace

- Anomalous military service established in 1995. - Joint-Venture between former Serpent's Hand operative Li Siben and former GoC agent Valentina de Oliveira Martins. - Usually not directly involved in conflicts but provides security for war zones and convoys and military training. - Will employ all sorts of anomalies in their work without care for the veil. - Strained relationship with the Foundation. - Will eradicate threats and save people as contracted.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Hong Kong Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macao, Singapore and Malaysia Unknown

- Company dealing in anomalous chemical products. - Known for their effectiveness and cheap production but also for the harm their products present to the users. - Only communicate in Traditional Chinese. - Use anomalies in their production processes. - Will cut communication after an order is finished, even memory wiping customers, contact has to be established again afterwards. - Indifferent towards the Foundation. - Doesn't care about any harm it causes.

entries.title: Mu Yi Private Library and Museum

profileContent.title: Mu Yi Private Library and Museum

blocks.text: Origin: Active in: Creator:: Taiwan Taiwan, Hong Kong minmasterqw

- Private Library and Museum for anomalous artifacts, found in 1978. - Established a branch in Hong Kong under the protection of the Foundation, allowing it to gain intel on anomalies and anomalies themselves. - Allowed to contain Safe Class anomalies. - Cooperates with the Foundation. - Wishes no harm to anybody.
8th Department of National Security Bureau, R. O. C.
The relationship is strained, as Mu Yi is competing with the Department for the recovery of ancient books and artifacts. It is unknown why the Department fears Mu Yi.
Division XXV
Mu Yi knows of Division XXV thanks to the Foundation and helps to trace the trafficking of its remains.
The Hive
The Library is wary of the Hive thanks to information gathered from the Foundation and only makes contact with many precautions.
Tsar's Seers
Both groups have a mutual assistance agreement, with Mu Yi handing over anomalies originally belonging to Russia.

entries.title: The 8th Department of National Security Bureau, R. O. C.

profileContent.title: The 8th Department of National Security Bureau, R. O. C.

blocks.text: Origin: Active in: Creator:: China the entire world Semibreve

- Former governmental organization destroyed during the Cold War by the GOC and the MI666 - Organization that has colonized locations in various parallel universes, highly militaristic. - Has only recently been discovered by the Foundation. - Also employs anomalous personnel in its ranks to heighten combat efficiency. - Tries to colonize our world also. - Hostile towards the Foundation. - If provoked, will annihilate any adversaries with maximum firepower, if necessary.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau Chromeblushowo

- Anomalous laundry and clothing maintenance service, also known as Camellia Laundry, Phantasm Orchid. - Will try to clean anything a customer might honestly consider as clothing. - Uses anomalous means to get clothes spotless. - The Foundation is a regular. - Will try to prevent accidents during laundry.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Russia Russia Reverberate_a

- Association of scholars of the anomalous, established in 1480 and officially disbanded in 1920. after the Revolution. - After disbandment some members lurked in other anomalous groups while the rest went into hiding. - Nowadays, about half of them have thaumaturgic capabilities. - Cooperates with the Foundation in exchange for protection. - Mostly harmless, even helping groups sheltering members.
YuanJhih Biomedicine Inc.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Taiwan Taiwan, Hong Kong, Shanghai SamScript

- Famous incorporation in normal Taiwan society. - Mainly devoted to medical services, R&D and education. - Viewing paranormal biological anomalies as new resources and applying them. - Barely aware of anomalous communities under the Veil. - A majority of their activities and employees are still considered normal by the Foundation.

entries.title: Zero Team, Royal Hong Kong Police

profileContent.title: Zero Team, Royal Hong Kong Police

blocks.text: Origin: Active in: Creator:: Hong Kong New Cha Ling, Hong Kong minmasterqw

- Police Force for the anomalous, formerly known as Colonial Police Force, founded in 1934 by the MI666. - Reorganised into the Cha Ling Police Department by the People's Republic of China in 1997. - Responsible for handling anomalous situations in New Cha Ling, Hong Kong. - Allowed to use several sorts of anomalies to do its job. - Hostile towards other religious groups. - Cooperates with the Foundation. - As their job entails, the officers try to keep people safe.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Unknown Russia Lalartu

- Variety of sects that worship entropy, in all its forms. - Entropy is anthropomorphized into the Gangrenous God and several smaller deities, the Permutation Portenders. - Religious practices include self-mutilation, voluntary infection and self-poisoning. - Make extensive use of anomalous artifacts for religious practices. - Neutral towards the Foundation, but causes a lot of problems. - Given their beliefs, they have no qualms regarding civilian casualties.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Russia Russia Teomant

- An inventor, well-versed in the creation of anomalies. - Provides criminal organisations with his devices and substances. - He claims his goods are of his own design, but this is not certain. - Leaves notes with his creations. - Neutral towards the Foundation. - Doesn't care what people do with his creations.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Russia Russia alpha9

- Originally a project of the Foundation and the GOC in the 1990s. - Due to turmoil between the Foundation and the GOC, Logos became independent and went rogue. - Pursues scientific advance in the fields of medicine, IT and psychology. - Hostile towards the Foundation.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: Russia Russia paranoik

- Collective of "artists" that practices reshaping of human bodies. - Possesses three departments with each having different methods of "art creation". - Each department aims to create the ultimate work of art, the "Masterpiece". - Hostile towards the Foundation. - Not above abducting and killing people in its pursuit of art.
Origin: Active in: Creator:: USSR USSR Arbelict

- Small research institute created in 1919 to research the anomalous and further attain the ideals of communism. - Was staffed with very idealistic researchers but they became gradually disillusioned thanks to the Soviet government. - On the 12th of July, 1988, the majority of the Institute started a Heist, stealing and destroying many of its creations to never be found again by the KGB. - Nowadays, remains of the Institute can be found on the black market. - Stance towards the Foundation is unknown. - Did not wish to inflict suffering, however, some research subjects experienced horrendous side-effects from experiments.
